drafts.after: God gives His Sabbaths as a lasting sign between Him and His people. The sign marks them as His own, so they know that He is the LORD who makes them holy. Genesis 2:1-3 and Exodus 20:8-11 stand behind this, and the Sabbath still marks out those who worship the Creator. First principle: sanctification is not self-righteous works; the Sabbath signifies resting from our own works in the finished work of the Creator and Redeemer, who makes them holy.
drafts.reason: V3: 'perpetual', 'identity marker', 'distinguishing' and 'Grounded in' are all decode-words. V2: the 27-word opener carried two ideas under one subject. Rebuilt as four plain sentences, each with one actor: God gives, the sign marks, Genesis and Exodus stand behind, and the LORD makes them holy. 'sanctifies them' is rendered as the glossary wording 'makes them holy', and 'permanent' becomes the everyday 'still'. Claims kept: the Sabbaths are God's gift; they are a sign between God and His people; the purpose is knowing the LORD; Gen 2:1-3 and Exod 20:8-11 are the grounding; the Sabbath still separates true worshipers of the Creator; the First principle clause is otherwise byte-identical. Citations Gen 2:1 and Exod 20:8 unchanged, none added.
